paragraphs.text: Terminal 1, the airport's main terminal, was officially inaugurated by King Salman on 24 September 2019. Arab News, citing the airport's website, gives it 46 boarding gates, a total area of 810,000 square metres and room for around 30 million passengers a year.

Terminal 4, the redeveloped former South Terminal, began phased operations on 27 September 2026, adding capacity for up to 15 million passengers a year. The airport also has the North Terminal and the Hajj and Umrah Terminals. King Abdulaziz International handled a record 53.4 million passengers in 2025.

The airport operator, Jeddah Airports Co. (JEDCO), plans to move all foreign airlines now at the North Terminal, and selected foreign airlines at Terminal 1 and the Hajj and Umrah Terminals, to Terminal 4. The first phase, from 27 September 2026, moved Wizz Air, AJet and SalamAir.

JEDCO's schedule for the following week: Fly Jinnah from the Hajj and Umrah Terminals' B3 facility and Nesma Airlines from the North Terminal on 28 September; Akasa Air from B3 on 29 September; SyrianAir and Pegasus from the North Terminal on 1 October; and Azerbaijan Airlines and Tunisair two days later. More airlines are to follow, so check the terminal on your booking before you travel.

sections.heading: Getting to and from the city

paragraphs.text: The airport has a station on the Haramain High Speed Railway, connected to Terminal 1. Saudi Gazette described it in December 2019 as a six-storey, 99,000-square-metre station with ticket vending machines and electronic gates, linking the airport with the Haramain train network to Madinah.

An express bus, run by the Jeddah Transport Company with Jeddah Airports Company and SAPTCO since April 2022, links Terminal 1 and the North Terminal with the SAPTCO station in Al-Balad. Stops on the way are near Flamingo Mall on Prince Majed Street, near Al-Andalus Mall, and Baghdadiya 7 on Madinah Road. In February 2023 the fare was SR20; tickets are sold at points inside the airport and in the SAPTCO app.

faqs.q: Which terminal is my flight at Jeddah airport?
faqs.a: It depends on the airline, and it is changing: since 27 September 2026 foreign airlines have been moving to the new Terminal 4 in phases, from the North Terminal and some from Terminal 1 and the Hajj and Umrah Terminals. Check the terminal on your booking.

faqs.q: Is there a train from Jeddah airport?
faqs.a: Yes. The airport has a Haramain High Speed Railway station connected to Terminal 1.
